full_judgment: 10. In the case of Mr. Momtaz Mallik Vs. The Taxing Officer, 20 DLR 599 (S.C.), the question was, what court fee was to be paid on filing an appeal against the award of an Arbitrator appointed under Section 7 of the then East Bengal (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 (East Bengal Act No. XIII of 1948), shortly the Act. Section 7(b) of the Act was in similar terms as in Section 27 of the Ordinance. The Arbitrator under the Act was to be a Judicial Officer not below the rank of a Subordinate Judge and was to be appointed by the then Provincial Government by notification in the official Gazette. A Special Bench of the then Dhaka High Court held in the aforesaid: case that the Arbitrator appointed under the Act, though a Judicial Officer, does not function as a Court and is a persona designata. It was further held by the Special Bench that the Arbitrator's award not being a decree, nor having the force of a decree, the award being merely executable under the Rules, Article 11 of the Second Schedule of the Limitation Act was applicable to the petitioner's memorandum of appeal.
